sources.title: Hawaii Department of Taxation: Withholding Tax (employer FAQ)
sources.verifiedBy: fetched directly from tax.hawaii.gov and read: payment frequency by withholding tax liability (greater than $40,000 semi-weekly, due Wednesday for wages paid the immediately preceding Wednesday, Thursday or Friday and Friday for wages paid the preceding Saturday through Tuesday; $5,000 to $40,000 monthly, the 15th of the month after the month; less than $5,000 quarterly, April 15, July 15, October 15, January 15); taxpayers with withholding liabilities over $40,000 must e-pay (a 2% penalty otherwise); employers whose annual withholding liability exceeds $40,000 must file all withholding forms, including W-2 and HW-2, electronically ($25 per form penalty up to $50 per employee, section 235-63 HRS).

efile.text: Employers whose annual withholding tax liability exceeds $40,000 must electronically file all withholding tax forms, including Forms W-2 and HW-2, regardless of the number filed; a penalty of $25 per form not filed electronically, up to $50 per employee, applies (section 235-63, HRS).

epay.text: Taxpayers with withholding tax liabilities over $40,000 must e-pay; failure to do so draws a 2% penalty of the tax required to be shown on the return.

returns.name: Form HW-14, Withholding Tax Return (quarterly return; periodic returns may be e-filed on Hawaii Tax Online)
contents: Filed by the 15th day of the month following the close of the filing period; Form VP-1 accompanies the remittance.
Periodic HW-14 returns, including amended returns, may be electronically filed, and payments made, on Hawaii Tax Online.

returns.name: Form HW-30, Employer's Annual Transmittal of Hawaii Income Tax Withheld from Wages
contents: Filed with copy A of the HW-2s or copy 1 of the federal W-2s; not needed when EFW-2 files are uploaded through Hawaii Tax Online, Simple File Import or the Bulk File System.
Employees receive HW-2 or W-2 copies by January 31; the State transmittal Form N-196 with federal 1099s is due by February 28 (29 in a leap year).

deposits.interpretation: Hawaii sets the remittance frequency from the ANNUAL State withholding liability: $5,000 or less QUARTERLY (Form VP-1 by the 15th day of the month following the quarter); more than $5,000 and not more than $40,000 MONTHLY (VP-1 by the 15th of the month following the month). Above $40,000 the Department's page (S2) states a SEMIWEEKLY schedule: wages paid Wednesday to Friday due the Wednesday after, Saturday to Tuesday the Friday after (the booklet adds the federal Three-Day Banking Rule's extra banking day, which is not applied because the state holiday list is unverified: weekends only). Hawaii does not use the federal four-quarter look-back. The frequency is otherwise an INPUT or derived from the annual liability supplied.

returns.name: Quarterly Wage, Contribution and Employment and Training Assessment Report (Form UC-B6)
contents: Due no later than April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31; filed each quarter even when no wages were paid.
A $30 penalty applies if the UC-B6 is not submitted on or before the last day of the month after the quarter; benefits-related consequences also apply (handbook).

Penalties: late contribution payment 10% but not less than $100, with interest of two-thirds of one percent a month on contributions and penalty unpaid 15 days after the due date; a late Form UC-B6 $30; a late separation report (Form UC-BP-35) $10 (handbook 'Penalties' section).
